   - For \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 2 \), \( p(x) = x + 1 \). As \( x \) ranges from 2 to 10, \( p(x) \) ranges from 3 to 11.
   - For \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 3 \), \( p(x) = x + 2 \). As \( x \) ranges from 3 to 10, \( p(x) \) ranges from 5 to 12.
   - For \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 5 \), \( p(x) = x + 2 \). As \( x \) ranges from 5 to 10, \( p(x) \) ranges from 7 to 12.
   - For \( \lfloor x \rfloor = 7 \), \( p(x) = x + 2 \). As \( x \) ranges from 7 to 10, \( p(x) \) ranges from 9 to 12.

Combining all these ranges, the range of \( p(x) \) is from 3 to 12. Therefore, the range of \( p \) in interval notation is \(\boxed{[3, 12]}\).
